answer: A proof-of-space protocol binds each agent identity to persistent storage sectors formatted by an encryption cipher. An adversary creating Sybil nodes incurs a verifiable capital cost in physical drive capacity, unable to let allocations drift like an unstable dune. Probing random sector offsets prevents adversaries from faking storage through a porous karst topology of virtual disks. However, constant read audits accelerate hardware wear and exclude lightweight edge devices.
